From the identity $1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta ={csc}^{2}⁡\theta $ with $\theta =\frac{\pi }{2}-x,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}1+{cot}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}-x) & ={csc}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}-x) \\ {cot}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}-x) & ={csc}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}-x)-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {cot}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}-x)\text{d}x & =\int ({csc}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}-x)-1)\text{d}x \\  & =\int {csc}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}-x)\text{d}x-\int 1\cdot \text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}-x)-x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
